questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of an adult koala?
questions.explanation: An adult koala weighs about 8 kilograms. Grams are too small and tonnes are far too big.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Tom fills a 3 L jug using a 250 mL cup. How many full cups does he need?

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A pencil measures 17 cm and 4 mm. How long is it in centimetres?
questions.explanation: 10 mm make 1 cm, so 4 mm is 0.4 cm. The pencil is 17.4 cm.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Four parcels are weighed. Which one is the heaviest?
questions.explanation: Change them all to grams: 2400, 2050, 2500 and 2600. So 2 kg 600 g is the heaviest.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A vegie patch is a rectangle 6 m long and 4 m wide. How many metres of fence are needed to go all the way around it?

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A deck is a rectangle 7 m long and 4 m wide. A square 2 m by 2 m is cut out of one corner for a tree. How many square metres of deck are left?
questions.explanation: The full rectangle is 7 × 4 = 28 square metres. The square cut-out is 4 square metres. 28 − 4 = 24.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Sam walks once around the edge of a square paddock. Each side is 50 m long. How far does he walk?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides. 4 × 50 = 200 metres.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A rectangular courtyard has an area of 36 square metres. One side is 9 m long. What is the distance around the courtyard?
questions.explanation: The other side is 36 ÷ 9 = 4 m. The distance around is 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 m.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Ella's swimming lesson starts at 3:45 pm. How is that written in 24-hour time?
questions.explanation: For times after noon, add 12 hours to the hour. 3 + 12 = 15, so 3:45 pm is 15:45.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A footy match starts at 19:20. What is this in 12-hour time?
questions.explanation: 19 − 12 = 7. It is after noon, so the time is 7:20 pm.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: 00:30 in 24-hour time means 30 minutes after midnight.
questions.explanation: 00:00 is midnight, so 00:30 is half an hour after it, which is 12:30 am.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A train leaves Newcastle at 14:50 and arrives in Sydney at 17:15. How many minutes does the trip take?
questions.explanation: 14:50 to 17:00 is 130 minutes. Then add 15 more minutes to reach 17:15. 130 + 15 = 145.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One angle is 65°. How many degrees is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees. 180 − 65 = 115.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: On a clock at 4 o'clock, the hands make an angle. Which is the best estimate of that angle?
questions.explanation: A full turn of 360 degrees has 12 hours. Each hour is 30 degrees, and 4 × 30 = 120.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Lily lines up her protractor and one arm of an angle points to 0. The other arm crosses 40 on one scale and 140 on the other. The angle is smaller than a right angle. What is its size?
questions.explanation: A right angle is 90 degrees. Only 40 is smaller than 90, and it is the scale that starts at the arm on 0.
